description: Tavuk Sis is a beloved Turkish classic featuring succulent pieces of chicken marinated in a vibrant yogurt and spice blend, then skewered and grilled to juicy perfection. This recipe brings the authentic flavors of Turkish street food right to your kitchen, offering a delightful culinary experience. Perfect for a family meal or entertaining guests, these flavorful skewers are sure to impress.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

ingredients.notes: soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes if using

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Cut the chicken breast or thigh into uniform 1-inch cubes. Pat them dry with paper towels to ensure the marinade adheres well. Set aside in a large bowl.

instructions.title: Make the Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate medium bowl, combine the yogurt, olive oil, tomato paste, minced garlic, grated onion, sweet paprika, dried oregano, cumin powder, salt, black pepper, and lemon juice. Whisk everything together until you have a smooth and well-combined marinade.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken cubes to the marinade, ensuring every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to deeply penetrate the chicken. This step is crucial for tender and flavorful skewers.

instructions.title: Skewer the Chicken
instructions.text: If using wooden skewers, ensure they have been soaked in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning. Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto the skewers, packing them gently but not too tightly. Leave a small space between each piece to ensure even cooking.

instructions.title: Preheat and Grill
instructions.text: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (about 400-450°F or 200-230°C). Lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking. Place the skewers on the hot grill. You can also cook these in a hot oven or under a broiler.

instructions.title: Cook the Skewers
instructions.text: Grill the Tavuk Sis for 15-20 minutes, turning them every 4-5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, golden brown, and has nice char marks. The internal temperature should reach 165°F (74°C). Do not overcook to keep the chicken juicy.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist chicken. Serve hot with your favorite Turkish sides.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, allow the chicken to marinate overnight. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful your Tavuk Sis will be.
Do not skip the grated onion in the marinade; it adds a subtle sweetness and helps tenderize the chicken. You can strain the onion juice for a smoother marinade if preferred.
Serve Tavuk Sis with traditional Turkish accompaniments like pilaf rice, a fresh shepherd's salad (Çoban Salata), lavash bread, and a dollop of cooling cacık (yogurt-cucumber dip).
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the vibrant streets of Turkey, where the tantalizing aroma of grilled meats fills the air. Among the most beloved and iconic dishes is Tavuk Sis, succulent chicken skewers that epitomize the rich flavors and grilling traditions of Turkish cuisine. This delightful dish, found everywhere from bustling street food stalls to elegant restaurants, is a testament to simple ingredients transformed into an extraordinary meal. If you're looking to bring authentic Turkish flavors into your kitchen, mastering Tavuk Sis is a fantastic place to start. It’s a dish that promises tender, juicy chicken bursting with Mediterranean spices, perfect for any gathering or a special weeknight dinner.

## What is Tavuk Sis Chicken Skewers?

Tavuk Sis, literally translating to "chicken shish," refers to marinated cubes of chicken threaded onto skewers and grilled to perfection. It's the chicken counterpart to the more famous Adana or Urfa kebabs, but instead of ground meat, it features tender chunks of chicken, usually breast or thigh meat. The magic of Tavuk Sis lies primarily in its marinade – a creamy, tangy, and aromatic blend of yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and a medley of Turkish spices like paprika, oregano, and cumin. This marinade not only infuses the chicken with incredible flavor but also acts as a tenderizer, ensuring each bite is moist and succulent. When grilled over charcoal, the chicken develops a beautiful char and smoky depth that is simply irresistible. It’s a dish celebrated for its balanced flavors, healthy profile, and universal appeal, making it a staple in Turkish homes and a favorite among international food enthusiasts.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Tavuk Sis begins with selecting fresh, quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need to gather for this sensational Turkish chicken recipe:

For the Chicken:
*   **1.5 lbs (about 700g) Boneless, Skinless Chicken Thighs or Breasts:** Thighs are often preferred for their higher fat content, which keeps them juicier. Cut into 1-inch cubes.

For the Marinade:
*   **½ cup Plain Full-Fat Yogurt:** Greek yogurt works wonderfully for a thicker marinade.
*   **¼ cup Olive Oil:** Good quality extra virgin olive oil for flavor.
*   **2 tablespoons Fresh Lemon Juice:** Adds brightness and helps tenderize.
*   **4-5 cloves Garlic:** Minced or grated for a pungent aroma.
*   **1 tablespoon Sweet Paprika:** For color and mild sweetness. Smoked paprika can add depth.
*   **1 teaspoon Dried Oregano:** A classic Mediterranean herb.
*   **½ teaspoon Ground Cumin:** Earthy and warm, essential for Turkish flavor.
*   **½ teaspoon Black Pepper:** Freshly ground preferred.
*   **1 teaspoon Salt:** Adjust to taste.
*   **½ teaspoon Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber) (Optional):** For a subtle kick.

Other Essentials:
*   **Wooden or Metal Skewers:** If using wooden skewers, remember to soak them in water beforehand.
*   **Optional Vegetables for Skewering:** Bell peppers (various colors), red onion, cherry tomatoes, zucchini, cut into 1-inch pieces.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these simple steps to create delicious Tavuk Sis in your own kitchen:

**Step 1: Prepare the Chicken**
Pat your chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Cut the chicken into uniform 1-inch cubes. Uniform pieces ensure even cooking.

**Step 2: Make the Marinade**
In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, paprika, oregano, cumin, black pepper, salt, and red pepper flakes (if using). Ensure all ingredients are well combined to form a smooth, aromatic paste.

**Step 3: Marinate the Chicken**
Add the cubed chicken to the bowl with the marinade. Toss thoroughly until every piece of chicken is fully coated. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours). The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful your Tavuk Sis will be.

**Step 4: Skewer the Chicken**
If using wooden skewers, ensure they have been soaked in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning. Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto the skewers. If adding vegetables, alternate chicken pieces with bell peppers, onions, or tomatoes for added flavor and visual appeal. Don't overcrowd the skewers; leave a little space between pieces for even cooking.

**Step 5: Preheat Your Grill or Oven**
*   **Grill:** Preheat your charcoal or gas grill to medium-high heat (around 400-450°F / 200-230°C). If using charcoal, wait until the coals are ash-gray and glowing.
*   **Oven Broiler:** Position an oven rack about 6-8 inches from the broiler element. Preheat the broiler on high. Line a baking sheet with foil for easier cleanup.

**Step 6: Cook the Tavuk Sis**
*   **Grilling:** Place the skewers on the preheated grill. Cook for 8-12 minutes, turning them every 2-3 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, no longer pink in the center, and has beautiful char marks on all sides.
*   **Broiling:** Place the skewers on the prepared baking sheet. Broil for 10-15 minutes, flipping them every 3-4 minutes, until the chicken is golden brown, cooked through, and slightly charred.

**Step 7: Rest and Serve**
Once cooked, remove the Tavuk Sis from the heat and let them rest for 5 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring the chicken remains succulent.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving perfect Tavuk Sis consistently involves a few key techniques:

*   **Don't Skimp on Marination Time:** This is arguably the most crucial step. The yogurt and lemon juice work wonders in tenderizing the chicken, while the spices infuse deep flavor. Longer is always better here.
*   **Choose Your Chicken Wisely:** While chicken breast is lean, chicken thighs tend to stay juicier and more forgiving if slightly overcooked.
*   **Soak Wooden Skewers:** This prevents them from burning on the grill, especially important for longer cooking times.
*   **Evenly Cut Chicken:** Ensure all chicken pieces are roughly the same size (1-inch cubes) so they cook uniformly.
*   **Don't Overcrowd Skewers:** Leave a little breathing room between chicken pieces. This allows heat to circulate, promoting even cooking and better charring.
*   **Maintain Grill Temperature:** Cook over medium-high heat. Too low, and the chicken will dry out before charring; too high, and it will burn on the outside before cooking through.
*   **Resist Constant Flipping:** Let the skewers cook undisturbed for a few minutes on each side to develop a good sear and char.
*   **Rest the Chicken:** Just like steaks, resting the chicken after cooking allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in more tender and flavorful meat.

## Serving Suggestions

Tavuk Sis is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a range of traditional Turkish accompaniments. Here are some popular serving suggestions to complete your meal:

*   **Turkish Pilaf Rice:** A buttery, flavorful rice dish often made with orzo pasta.
*   **Lavash or Pita Bread:** Soft, warm flatbreads are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its juices.
*   **Çoban Salata (Shepherd's Salad):** A refreshing salad made with finely diced tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and bell peppers, dressed with olive oil and lemon juice.
*   **Cacık (Turkish Tzatziki):** A cool and creamy yogurt dip with grated cucumber, garlic, and fresh mint. It provides a lovely contrast to the grilled chicken.
*   **Ezme Salad:** A spicy, finely chopped tomato and pepper salad with walnuts and pomegranate molasses.
*   **Grilled Vegetables:** Skewered vegetables like bell peppers, onions, and tomatoes, grilled alongside the chicken.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Fresh Parsley:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors, and chopped parsley adds freshness and color.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Tavuk Sis recipe is fantastic, there's always room for personal touches and dietary adjustments:

*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) to your preference for more or less heat. You can also add a pinch of sumac for a tangy, lemony note.
*   **Herb Variations:** While oregano is traditional, try experimenting with fresh mint or dill in the marinade for a different aromatic profile.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** If you can't use yogurt, you can omit it and increase the olive oil and lemon juice slightly. A dairy-free yogurt alternative (like coconut yogurt, unsweetened) could also work, though it might impart a subtle flavor.
*   **Different Meats:** The same marinade can be used for lamb (Kuzu Şiş) or even firm fish. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Cooking Methods:** If you don't have a grill, you can bake the skewers in the oven (at 400°F/200°C for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway) or pan-fry the chicken pieces in a skillet until cooked through and nicely browned.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Feel free to add other vegetables to your skewers, such as mushrooms, zucchini, or even small potatoes, keeping in mind they may require slightly different cooking times.

Tavuk Sis is more than just a meal; it's an experience. The vibrant flavors, the smoky char, and the tender texture come together to create a dish that is both comforting and exhilarating. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook venturing into Turkish cuisine for the first time, this recipe is incredibly rewarding. So, fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and prepare to delight your taste buds with this unforgettable Turkish delicacy. Afiyet Olsun! (Enjoy your meal!)
